data.exact_reserve_text: The prior year development for 2022 is calculated from the 'Analysis of claims development gross' table on page 18, summing the changes in ultimate gross claims estimates for underwriting years 2013 to 2020. This results in a net release of GBP 31.402m.

prior_year_events.event_name: Russian invasion of Ukraine / Western leased aircraft
prior_year_events.impact_description: Gross strengthening of GBP 128.619m for the 2021 year of account due to trapped ships and destroyed buildings, and potential losses from western leased aircraft. This represents 93% of the total indirect losses of GBP 138.3m gross.

named_events.loss_description: Incurred claims in Marine War, Aviation War, Terrorism and Marine Reinsurance accounts mostly due to trapped ships and destroyed buildings. Total reserves amount to GBP 21.1m gross and GBP 8.7m net of reinsurance for direct losses, and GBP 138.3m gross and GBP 39.2m net of reinsurance for indirect losses, with 93% split to 2021 year of account and 7% to 2022 year of account.

Further possible loss that could surpass current Ukraine war reserves, extremely complicated situation with evidential picture still developing. Loss reserve split 93% to 2021 year of account and 7% to 2022 year of account.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced an overall prior year reserve release of GBP 31.402m in 2022, primarily due to favorable claims development across older underwriting years. However, this was partially offset by adverse development related to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which resulted in a gross strengthening of GBP 128.619m for the 2021 year of account, impacting Marine War, Aviation War, Terrorism, and Marine/Aviation Reinsurance lines due to trapped ships and destroyed buildings, and potential losses from western leased aircraft.
raw_causal_phrases: The largest loss event to occur in 2022 was the Russian invasion of Ukraine in February. We have incurred claims in our Marine War, Aviation War, Terrorism and Marine Reinsurance accounts mostly due to trapped ships and destroyed buildings. At year end our total reserves amount to GBP 21.1m gross and GBP 8.7m net of reinsurance. There is a further possible loss though that could surpass this - the fate of the western leased aircraft in Russia. This is an extremely complicated situation and one in which the evidential picture is still developing. ... The loss reserve is split 93% to the 2021 year of account and 7% to the 2022 year of account.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: The overall prior year development is a release based on the claims development triangle. However, specific prior year adverse development related to the Russian invasion of Ukraine for the 2021 year of account is also noted. The narrative regarding Florida contractors and General Liability deterioration was found in the 2020 closed year of account report, not the 2022 calendar year report, and was therefore excluded from the primary causes for the 2022 calendar year.
